# Brick Collisions 💥

#### Course: Brick Breaker with JavaScript

## Brick Collisions 💥

Brick collision needs to detect not just whether the ball hit a brick, but which side — so the ball bounces correctly. The technique calculates penetration depth on all four edges:

```javascriptDOM
const oL = br - brick.x;               // overlap from brick's left side
const oR = brick.x + brick.width - bl; // overlap from brick's right side

const oT = bb - brick.y;               // overlap from brick's top
const oB = brick.y + brick.height - bt;// overlap from brick's bottom
```

The collision came from the side with the smallest overlap — that is the surface the ball was nearest to when it entered:

```javascriptDOM
const m = Math.min(oL, oR, oT, oB);

if (m === oT) return "top";
if (m === oB) return "bottom";

return m === oL ? "left" : "right";
```

Then bounce: top and bottom hits flip ballSpeedY, left and right hits flip ballSpeedX. A break after the first hit prevents the ball from tunneling through multiple bricks in one frame.
